status: DRAFT 2026-11-14. Format and content are proposals; every item under 'choices' is undecided.

format.term: A string. '?name' is a variable; anything else is a prefixed name from 'prefixes'.
format.triple: A list of three terms: subject, predicate, object.
format.conclusion: A triple, or the string 'BOT' for an incompatibility.
format.defeaters: A list of graphs, each a list of triples. The entry instance applies when its premises are in K and no defeater has an instance contained in K. Variables of a defeater that do not occur in the premises are existential.
format.guards: Comparisons between literals bound by the premises.
format.expand: The entry stands for one entry per listed value of the variable.
format.variant_of: Entries sharing this value are alternatives; exactly one is to be kept.

choices: The regime is these two rules and nothing else. Alternative: no rules, with instance-of already closed under subclass-of in the selected subset.
Reading P31 and P279 as rdf:type and rdfs:subClassOf is ours. It is what the subject type constraint's relation 'instance of' (Q21503252) asks the checker to do.
Reading a symmetric-constraint violation as a default consequence is our stipulation; Wikidata documents constraints as hints for editors.
No defeater, because the constraint statement lists no exception. Alternative: the same exception defeater as the P47 entry, read from the constraint statement, which matches nothing on P26 today.
No status is stated on the constraint, so it is taken as defeasible. With no defeater the only effect of that is that the conclusion is added in the one round of entries and is not in K.

The entry applies when ?y is an unknown value (a Skolem IRI). No guard may exclude that case, since a guard may not depend on the identity of a Skolem term. The conclusion then has a Skolem IRI as subject.

choices: A type constraint is violated by the absence of a type, so it is written as an incompatibility whose defeaters are the allowed types: incompatible unless typed. This is our encoding.
It depends on the regime's two rules, or on a subset in which instance-of is already closed under subclass-of.
P26 has no value type constraint. This entry therefore constrains ?x and not ?y, which is the asymmetry between asserted and reverse direction.
Over the conclusions of p26-symmetric this entry would apply to every unknown-value spouse, since a Skolem IRI has no type.
evidence: results/p26-constraint-qualifiers/20261114T153135Z.json: the seven classes and the relation 'instance of'.
results/p26-constraints/20261114T153132Z.json: no value type constraint among the eleven.

choices: Only date of birth and date of death are compared. The constraint is believed, from documentation, to use inception and start time, and dissolved and end time, as well.
Direct date values carry no precision, so a year-precision date appears as 1 January. Comparing them as written over-reports; comparing years only is the alternative.
When either date is absent the entry does not apply. That this matches the checker is from documentation, not confirmed.
The check has no direction, so the pair p26-contemporary-subject-first and p26-contemporary-value-first together express it. A violation is therefore present at K whichever direction is asserted.
evidence: results/p26-nonoverlapping-lifetimes/20261114T153244Z.json: 200 rows (the cap), 184 distinct pairs; in 122 rows one date falls on 1 January.
